# Representations generated by fixed vectors: duality and the Hecke algebra (statements)

Author: Worker 6. Module `Langlands.Representation.Jacquet.FixedVectorCategoryStatements`, namespace `Langlands.Jacquet`, universes `uF` (field and group schemes) and `uV` (representation carriers).

The source is David Renard, *Représentations des groupes réductifs p-adiques*, French edition dated 9 July 2026, VI.10.6, Proposition (iii)–(iv) and their proofs, printed p.214 / PDF p.220. The registered source ID is `renard-2026-representations-groupes-reductifs-padiques`, SHA256 `7b539996793b7c3620e72e1e389588eb42d1a8e91d6f68b2eead5c2e2ffc182c`.

This is a statement unit: nothing is proved.

## The source

**Proposition.** Let `K` be a compact open subgroup of `G`, contained and normal in `K₀` and having an Iwahori decomposition along the standard parabolic subgroups.

- (i) The subcategory `M(G)_K` of representations generated by their `K`-invariant vectors is closed under subquotients, and `M(G)_K ≃ ∏_{𝔰 ∈ B(G)_K} M(G)_𝔰`.
- (ii) The functor `V ↦ V^K` is an equivalence of `M(G)_K` with `M(H(G, K))`, with inverse `M ↦ H(G) ⊗_{H(G,K)} M`.
- (iii) For every `(π, V) ∈ M(G)`, `(π, V) ∈ M(G)_K` if and only if `(π̃, Ṽ) ∈ M(G)_K`.
- (iv) The algebra `H(G, K)` is Noetherian.

The proof of (iii) splits `Ṽ = W₁ + W₂` along the decomposition of (i), with `W₁` generated by `Ṽ^K`, and shows `W₂ = 0`. The converse uses `V ↪ Ṽ̃`. For (iv), each `M(G)_𝔰` is a Noetherian category, so `M(G)_K` and hence `M(H(G, K))` are Noetherian, and `H(G, K)` is of finite type over itself.

## The Lean statement

`FixedVectorCategoryStatements` has exactly the data and hypotheses of the published VI.9.4 statements `StandardFixedVectorSubquotientGenerationStatement` and `StandardFixedVectorHeckeEquivalenceStatement` (Worker 6), whose Markdown describes them in detail.

- `F` is a nonarchimedean local field and `G` a connected reductive group scheme over `Spec F`, with the topology `rationalPointTopology F G.X` on `G(F)`.
- `i : S.toGrp ⟶ G` is a maximal split torus and `ν` a generic cocharacter, fixing the minimal parabolic and the standard parabolics, with the standard-cocharacter input `_hstandard`.
- `K₀` is a compact subgroup with the Iwasawa factorization `G(F) = M_∅(F) N_∅(F) K₀`.
- `K` is a compact open subgroup with `K ≤ K₀` and `K₀ ≤ normalizer K`, i.e. contained and normal in `K₀`.
- `_hIwahori`: for every standard index `J`, `K` is a member of the V.5.2 basis along the standard parabolic of `J`, through the published `StandardParabolicBasisMember`. This includes the Iwahori decomposition `K = (K ∩ N̄_J)(K ∩ M_J)(K ∩ N_J)`.

"Generated by its `K`-fixed vectors" is `fixedVectorGenerated K.toSubgroup V`: every subrepresentation `T` of `V` whose underlying submodule contains the `K`-fixed vectors is all of `V`. This reuses the predicate in `Jacquet/FixedVectorGeneratedCategory` and is the formulation of the VI.9.4 statements.

The conclusion is the conjunction of:

1. **(iii)** For every `V : SmoothRep.{0, uF, uV} ℂ (rationalPoints G)`, `fixedVectorGenerated K.toSubgroup V ↔ fixedVectorGenerated K.toSubgroup V.contragredient`. Here `V.contragredient` is the published smooth contragredient (module `Category/Contragredient`): the smooth linear functionals with the contragredient action, again in carrier universe `uV`.
2. **(iv)** `IsNoetherianRing H` and `IsNoetherianRing Hᵐᵒᵖ` for `H = Shimura.LevelHecke.LevelHeckeAlgebra ℂ K`, the published Hecke algebra `ℂ[G(F)/K]^K` of `K`. The first says that `H` is left Noetherian, the second that it is right Noetherian. The same Hecke algebra is used by the published VI.9.4 Proposition.

## Remarks

- `LevelHeckeAlgebra` is normalized by counting measure on `G(F)/K`. Renard's `H(G, K) = e_K ∗ H(G) ∗ e_K` uses a Haar measure. The two algebras are isomorphic by rescaling functions by `vol(K)`, so Noetherianity does not depend on the normalization.
- Renard's argument gives left Noetherianity: `M(H(G, K))` is the category of left modules. Right Noetherianity is included because the anti-automorphism `f ↦ (g ↦ f(g⁻¹))` of `H(G, K)`, valid as `G(F)` is unimodular, identifies `H(G, K)` with its opposite ring. Renard does not specify a side.
- (i), first assertion, is the published VI.9.4 Corollary `StandardFixedVectorSubquotientGenerationStatement`. (ii) is the published VI.9.4 Proposition `StandardFixedVectorHeckeEquivalenceStatement`, which asserts that `V ↦ V^K` is an equivalence. The inverse functor `M ↦ H(G) ⊗_{H(G,K)} M` is not stated.
- The decomposition `M(G)_K ≃ ∏_{𝔰 ∈ B(G)_K} M(G)_𝔰` of (i) needs the Bernstein decomposition VI.7.2 and is not stated here. The finiteness of `B(G)_K` and the description of `Ω(G)_K` as a union of components are the VI.10.6 Theorem, stated by Worker 6 as `CompactOpenInertialFinitenessStatement`.
- The proofs are not formalized here.
